User.title: User
User.description: Represents a user of the RAFA Project Launcher.

GameRequest.title: GameRequest
GameRequest.description: Represents a request for a game on the RAFA Project Launcher.

id.description: Unique identifier for the game request.

userId.description: Reference to the User who made the request. (Relationship: User 1:N GameRequest)

gameName.description: The name of the game being requested.

platform.description: The platform the game is requested for (PC, PS4/5, Xbox, Switch).

notes.description: Any additional notes or comments from the user.

requestDate.description: The date and time the request was submitted.

AvailableGame.title: AvailableGame
AvailableGame.description: Represents a game that is available on the RAFA Project Launcher.

id.description: Unique identifier for the available game.

name.description: The name of the available game.

supportedPlatforms.description: List of platforms supported by the game.

imageUrl.description: URL to the image of the game.

UserMessage.title: UserMessage
UserMessage.description: Represents a message sent between users within the RAFA Project Launcher.

senderId.description: Reference to the User who sent the message. (Relationship: User 1:N UserMessage - Sent)

receiverId.description: Reference to the User who received the message. (Relationship: User 1:N UserMessage - Received)

timestamp.description: The date and time the message was sent.

isRead.description: Indicates whether the message has been read by the receiver.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to be secure, scalable, and easily debuggable, following the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). It leverages denormalization and structural segregation to simplify security rules and ensure data integrity.

**Authorization Independence:**  Authorization independence is achieved primarily through structural choices. User-owned data, like `GameRequest` and `UserMessage` are stored under the `/users/{userId}` path.  This path-based ownership inherently provides authorization independence because access control can be determined directly from the path without needing to `get()` data from other collections.

**Structural Segregation:** All documents within a collection share the same security requirements. For instance, `GameRequest` is stored as a subcollection of `/users/{userId}/game_requests/{gameRequestId}` to ensure only the user can access their own game requests. `AvailableGame` are stored in `/available_games/{availableGameId}` to allow any user to read it but only admins can write.

**Access Modeling:**
*   **Private Data:** `/users/{userId}/game_requests/{gameRequestId}` and `/users/{userId}/messages/{messageId}` demonstrates path-based ownership for user-specific data.

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
*   The structure supports secure `list` operations because collections are segregated based on access requirements.  Listing game requests under `/users/{userId}/game_requests` only requires checking `request.auth.uid == userId`.

**Invariants:**
*   Ownership of `GameRequest` and `UserMessage` is enforced by the path and secured by rules based on `request.auth.uid`.
